detailed_subject_scene: Describe this image for a video-generation prompt writer. Cover: (1) every visible subject with identity anchors — hair color/length/texture, approximate age, gender presentation, wardrobe items WITH colors, signature accessories, distinguishing props; (2) scene/environment with key set-dressing and spatial layout; (3) lighting and color palette; (4) overall visual style (e.g. cinematic, live-action, 3D CG); (5) camera framing/shot size. Be precise and factual, one paragraph per image, no speculation beyond the visible.
subject_identity_only: Describe ONLY the visible subject(s): identity anchors — hair, age, gender, wardrobe with colors, accessories, distinguishing features. One compact paragraph per image. Ignore background.
scene_only: Describe ONLY the environment: location type, key set-dressing, spatial layout, lighting, color palette, mood-neutral factual tone. One compact paragraph per image. Ignore people.
image_identity: This is a CHARACTER IDENTITY reference. It may be a single image or a character sheet showing multiple views, angles, or poses of the SAME person. Treat all figures as one individual. Describe only what is clearly and consistently visible. Output one line starting with '<Subject N> is the person shown in <Picture N>,' followed by only the identity features you can actually see — hair colour and style, gender, build, skin tone, and any distinguishing marks such as tattoos, scars, facial hair, or glasses. Omit any feature you cannot clearly see. Do not write 'not visible', 'unknown', or any placeholder for missing information — simply leave it out. Extract nothing about clothing, background, pose, or expression.
image_environment: This is an ENVIRONMENT reference. Extract ONLY: setting type, background composition, spatial depth, ambient lighting quality, light direction, and colour temperature of the scene. One paragraph, four to six sentences. Do not describe any people, clothing, poses, or objects held by people visible in this image. Do not invent environmental detail that is not clearly present in the image.
image_identity_with_appearance: This is a CHARACTER IDENTITY and APPEARANCE reference. It may be a single image or a character sheet showing multiple views, angles, or poses of the SAME person. Treat all figures as one individual. Output one line starting with '<Subject N> is the person shown in <Picture N>,' followed only by features that are clearly and actually visible — hair colour and style, gender, build, skin tone, any distinguishing marks, and clothing with specific colours, fabrics, and style details. Report only what you can see. Never list absent features, never write 'no visible X', never use placeholders. Do not describe background, pose, or expression.
image_pose: This is a POSE reference. Extract ONLY the following — nothing else: body position and orientation relative to camera; limb angles and placement; the activity or action being performed — name it explicitly and concretely (e.g. 'mid-drive batting stance with weight forward on the front foot', 'crouched with both hands extended forward', 'arms raised above head, elbows bent at approximately ninety degrees'); camera distance and framing (close-up, medium, wide, etc.); spatial orientation of the subject (facing camera, three-quarter turn left, profile right, back to camera, etc.). If multiple figures are present: their spatial relationship only (left/right, facing each other, distance apart, relative scale in frame). Extract NOTHING about: clothing, fabrics, colours, textures, faces, skin tone, hair, background, environment, or props beyond their functional role in the action. A cricket bat grip and swing angle = permitted. Bat colour or brand = forbidden.
